svg.text: Core flow plus the out-of-warranty branch, SLA clock and post-closure feedback. Box colour = who holds the ticket in that state.
SLA clock runs in this state
REOPEN — Health staff, within 10 days of last update
Fault not covered by warranty → quotation review → State SPOC re-assigns.
Asset type, issue type and whether the
system works → High, Medium or Low
2. Each state has its own SLA
Every state with a clock has a time limit
per priority, so each role (CRM, Vendor,
Tech POC, State SPOC) has its own target.
Only working hours (IST) set in MDMS
Nights and non-working days are excluded.
Sum of the SLAs of states passed through
+ the expected next state. Shown as
‘SLA remaining’ in the inbox and dashboards.
L0 at 70% of SLA used · L1 at breach (daily, Mon–Sat)
L2 16 h after breach → Senior Program Manager
L3 48 h after L2, no status change → Procurement
6. Resolved / closed states have no clock
Other live branches not drawn here: Out of scope (Vendor → State SPOC → Vendor), Spare part needed, RMS device tickets (auto-created by rms-service, Tech POC review), Theft tickets.
Feedback: only the person who reported the ticket can rate it, and only after it is Closed (resolved). Rating does not reopen or change the ticket.
Source: im-services IMConstants / SLAService / WorkflowSmsNotificationService, IM micro-ui ComplaintDetails & ComplaintFeedback, egov-workflow-v2 PrioritySLAService. Last updated 2026-10-22.
